title: When God feels silent
speaker: Pastor Michelle
blurb: The Psalms are full of people asking God how long. Not one of them is rebuked for it. The first message in a short series about the stretches of faith nobody puts on a testimony video.
takeaways: "How long?" is a prayer. It is in the Bible four times in the first two verses of this psalm.
Silence is not the same as absence, and treating them as the same is what turns a hard season into a lost one.
David ends the psalm singing without having received an answer. The singing is the point.
question: What have you stopped bringing to God because you got no answer the first time?

title: The waiting room
speaker: Pastor Jason
blurb: Habakkuk asks a question and then does something most of us never do: he says where he will be standing while he waits for the answer.
takeaways: Waiting is a place you stand, not a thing that happens to you.
Habakkuk keeps his post. Faith is often just refusing to leave.
The answer, when it comes, is written down so it can outlive the mood it was received in.
question: Where is your post — the place you keep turning up to, whether or not anything is happening there?

title: Enough for the day
speaker: Pastor Michelle
blurb: The most-quoted verse in the book is in the middle of the saddest chapter in the Bible. That is not an accident, and it is not a contradiction either.
takeaways: Mercy is described as new every morning — a day's worth, not a lifetime's supply.
The writer is not describing a good week. He is describing what is still true in a bad one.
"Great is your faithfulness" is a statement about God, not a report on how you feel.
question: What would change this week if you only asked God for today?

title: Built on the rock
speaker: Pastor Jason
blurb: Both houses in the parable get the same storm. The difference is not the weather — it is what was done before the weather arrived.
takeaways: Jesus does not promise a smaller storm to the wise builder.
The foundation is laid in the ordinary weeks, which is why the ordinary weeks matter.
Hearing and doing are one act in this parable. Hearing alone builds on sand.
question: What have you heard from God more than once and not yet acted on?

title: A church away from home
speaker: Pastor Michelle
blurb: Peter writes to people scattered across five provinces, working far from where they were born. He calls them chosen, not stranded.
takeaways: The New Testament church was largely a migrant church. This is not a modern problem the Bible has nothing to say about.
Belonging somewhere is not the same as being from somewhere.
A church you joined as a stranger is still your church.
question: Who here would notice if you stopped coming — and who would you notice?

title: The people you did not choose
speaker: Elder Ruth
blurb: You choose your friends. You do not choose your church. That is the difficulty and it is also the whole point.
takeaways: Honour is something you give first, not something you wait to be given.
A congregation you assembled from people you already liked would teach you nothing.
The instruction is affection, not tolerance. Those are different jobs.
question: Who in this church would you find it hardest to honour, and what would honouring them look like on Friday?

title: Communion is not a ceremony
speaker: Pastor Jason
blurb: On the first Friday of every month we do a very small thing very deliberately. This message is about why the size of it is the point.
takeaways: It is a proclamation, not a private moment — the table is a sermon the whole church preaches together.
"Until he comes" makes it a temporary practice. That is meant to be a comfort.
Coming to the table unreconciled with someone in the room is the one warning Paul gives about it.
question: Is there anyone in this church you would rather not sit at the table beside?

title: What you send home
speaker: Pastor Michelle
blurb: Most of this church works to support people in another country. This message is about doing that without being consumed by it.
takeaways: Providing for your family is named as an act of faith, not a distraction from it.
Providing is not the same as rescuing. Some things money genuinely cannot fix, and pretending otherwise will break you.
You are permitted to have needs of your own. A depleted person provides badly.
question: What are you carrying financially that you have never actually prayed about, only worried about?

title: Working for someone difficult
speaker: Elder Ruth
blurb: Paul wrote this to people with far less say over their working conditions than we have. That is exactly why it is worth reading slowly.
takeaways: The verse redirects who you are working for. It does not say the employer is right.
Doing work well is available to you even where justice is not.
This is not a command to stay silent about mistreatment. It is a command about your own soul while you are in it.
question: What part of your work have you let go of because nobody would notice?

title: Enough
speaker: Pastor Jason
blurb: Paul says contentment is something he learned. If it is learned, it can be learned by you, and it did not come naturally to him either.
takeaways: Contentment is a skill with a curriculum, and the curriculum includes going without.
He has learned it in plenty as well as in need. Both are hard, in different ways.
The strength in the verse after this one is strength to be content, not strength to get more.
question: What figure in your head counts as enough — and where did that figure come from?
